content.summary: Research findings for: thinking option error with opencode/kimi-k2.5

data.original_input: Investigate error when the thinking option is used with opencode/kimi-k2.5, focusing on thinking config, kimi-specific handling, model/provider config, and agent-specific thinking.

codebase_findings.details: Thinking options are validated via Config.Thinking (effort, budgetTokens) and referenced in Config.Agent. Agent loader copies the config into Agent.Info. LLM resolves agent.thinking into a ThinkingEffort and builds provider-specific thinking options for Anthropic/Bedrock/OpenAI/Azure/Copilot/Google/OpenRouter only; openai-compatible (opencode) is not handled, so agent thinking does not map to request options there.

Model variants are auto-generated only when model.capabilities.reasoning is true. For @ai-sdk/openai-compatible, variants map to reasoningEffort (low/medium/high). TUI/CLI store a per-model variant (labeled as thinking effort) and LLM merges variant options into request options.

ProviderTransform has Kimi-specific defaults: temperature for kimi-k2 and k2.* (k2.5) and topP for kimi-k2.5. The only explicit thinking enablement for Kimi is a chat_template_args.enable_thinking flag applied when providerID is opencode and model id is kimi-k2-thinking (or glm-4.6).

codebase_findings.topic: opencode provider and Kimi model definitions
codebase_findings.details: Bundled models snapshot defines provider opencode with npm @ai-sdk/openai-compatible and base URL https://opencode.ai/zen/v1. In the snapshot, opencode includes kimi-k2 (reasoning: false) and kimi-k2-thinking (reasoning: true, interleaved reasoning_content). No kimi-k2.5 appears in the bundled snapshot; if it exists at runtime, it comes from live models.dev data.

For models with interleaved reasoning fields, ProviderTransform normalizes assistant messages by lifting reasoning parts into providerOptions.openaiCompatible.<reasoning_field> and removing reasoning parts from content. This is the mechanism used for models like kimi-k2-thinking that mark interleaved reasoning_content.

The openai-compatible responses adapter only treats OpenAI o*/gpt-5/codex models as reasoning models; other model IDs are non-reasoning and will not include a reasoning object in request bodies, even if reasoningEffort is set. This can lead to reasoningEffort being ignored for non-OpenAI model IDs.

prior_art.summary: Earlier exploration documents agent frontmatter fields, including thinking, and notes unknown keys moved into options.

patterns: Thinking can come from two places: agent.thinking (provider-mapped options) and model variants (reasoning effort).
Kimi thinking enablement is currently special-cased only for kimi-k2-thinking via chat_template_args on the opencode provider.
opencode is an openai-compatible provider, so provider-specific options must map to openai-compatible expectations to take effect.
Bundled models snapshot may be stale; new model IDs (like kimi-k2.5) may only exist in live models.dev data.
raw_options: Inspect live models.dev (or cached models.json) to confirm opencode/kimi-k2.5 definition and reasoning/interleaved flags.
Reproduce the error with opencode/kimi-k2.5 + thinking effort enabled and capture request options/body to see which parameter triggers the failure.
Check whether opencode/kimi-k2.5 needs chat_template_args.enable_thinking (similar to kimi-k2-thinking) and whether that is missing.
Temporarily disable variants or mark k2.5 as non-reasoning to see if the error disappears (quick hypothesis test).
Verify providerOptions key mapping for openai-compatible (opencode) to ensure thinking-related options reach the provider.
Compare behavior with opencode/kimi-k2 vs opencode/kimi-k2-thinking to isolate which thinking path causes the error.
